_doc: PASA missions, offered in order once their 'after' missions are done. goal kinds: altitude (above sea level, m, at body), space (above the air at body), orbit (periapsis above the air at body), soi (in body's sphere of influence), landed (at body, not at Floe's launch site), eva_space (a penguin out in space), eva_landed (a penguin standing on body), recover_from (a craft that landed at body comes home), flag (a flag planted on body), rendezvous (within value m of another craft), docked, refine (making propellant away from Floe), hear (a Signal Scanner hears relic), investigate (a penguin on foot at relic), hover (value m above the ground, within band m, for seconds). hands_off: only if nobody touched the flying keys since liftoff (the ship's computer flew it). story is told when it is done.

missions.title: First hop
missions.text: Get a penguin 1 km up and back down.

missions.title: Touch space
missions.text: Climb above Floe's air (70 km).

missions.title: Orbit Floe
missions.text: Get into an orbit whose low point clears the air.

missions.title: Spacewalk
missions.text: Send a penguin outside in space (F).

missions.title: To Krill
missions.text: Reach Krill's sphere of influence.

missions.title: Land on Krill
missions.text: Set a craft down on Krill in one piece.

missions.title: Footprints
missions.text: A penguin standing on Krill.

missions.title: Flag on Krill
missions.text: Plant a PASA flag on Krill (a penguin on EVA presses G).

missions.title: Home from Krill
missions.text: Bring a craft that landed on Krill back to Floe and recover it.

missions.title: To Kelp
missions.text: Leave Floe behind and reach Kelp, the green world sunward of it.

missions.title: Land on Kelp
missions.text: Through Kelp's thick, hot air to the ground in one piece.

missions.title: Land on Pebble
missions.text: Kelp's little moon: set down on it (and mind the jump, its gravity is a twentieth of Floe's).

missions.title: Living off the land
missions.text: Land a drill, an ore bin and a refinery anywhere but Floe and make propellant there.

missions.title: To Narwhal
missions.text: Out past Floe to Narwhal, the cold blue world: a long coast round Austra.

missions.title: Land on Narwhal
missions.text: Its air is thin: a parachute alone won't save you. Bring an engine for the last of it.

missions.title: Land on Tusk
missions.text: Narwhal's bright little moon.

missions.title: The Hum
missions.text: PASA's big dish hears a slow, steady tone from Krill. Nothing natural sings like that. Research the Listening Post, then fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Krill's surface to pin the source down.
missions.story: There: a point on Krill's lowlands, south of the equator. The scanner holds a fix on it now; its heading and distance stay on your display whenever you are at Krill.

missions.title: The Chime
missions.text: Land near the source on Krill and walk a penguin right up to it.
missions.story: A ring of pale stone taller than any rocket PASA has flown, humming through the penguin's boots. At a touch the tone changes, and two new tones answer it from far away: one from Kelp, sunward, and one from Narwhal, out in the cold. Somebody built this, and they want to be found.

missions.title: The Warm Tone
missions.text: The answer from Kelp. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Kelp's surface to find it.
missions.story: Kelp's meadows, south of its equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Hearth
missions.text: Down through Kelp's thick air to the source, and a penguin to it.
missions.story: A low dome, warm to the flipper, and inside it a heart of light that never dims. The penguin's notes and PASA's engineers make a copy of sorts: the Hearth Core, a power source that runs on nothing anyone can name. It is yours to build with (R&D: The Hearth).

missions.title: The Deep Tone
missions.text: The answer from Narwhal. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Narwhal's surface to find it.
missions.story: Narwhal's plains, north of its equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Keel
missions.text: Land on Narwhal by the source and bring a penguin to it.
missions.story: The keel of a ship far bigger than anything PASA could lift, half buried in the ice. Its engine is still there, silent: it pushes every atom of a ship at once, so nobody aboard feels a thing however hard it drives. Its markings point at one star: Lantern, 4.2 light years away. With a Hearth Core to feed it, a Stillwater Drive could take penguins there (R&D: The Stillwater Drive).

missions.title: To Lantern
missions.text: Fly past Austra's heliopause (40 Gm out), set a course for Lantern and reach it. The trip is 4.2 years at home and only weeks aboard.
missions.story: A second sun. Lantern's light is warmer and dimmer than Austra's, and its worlds wait: Cinder close in, green Haven with its moon Wisp. And from Haven, a tone.

missions.title: The Last Tone
missions.text: Something on Haven answers the Chime too. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Haven's surface.
missions.story: Haven's grasslands, north of its equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Archive
missions.text: Land on Haven and walk a penguin to the source.
missions.story: Rows of standing stones, each holding the same map in light: the stars around Lantern and Austra, and a thread from star to star leading on, first to a dim red star, Ember, 3.6 light-years away, and from there much further. Whoever built the Chime came this way and kept going. The first penguins to cross between the stars stand here and hear the hum fade, westward, into the dark.

missions.title: To Ember
missions.text: The Archive's thread leads to Ember, a red dwarf 3.6 light-years from Lantern. Get out past Lantern's heliopause, set a course and follow it.
missions.story: Ember's light is the colour of a forge's last coals. One world, Gloam, keeps the same face to it forever: a hot desert under a sun that never moves, ice on the far side under stars that never set, and between them a ring of twilight. Something in the twilight is humming.

missions.title: Land on Gloam
missions.text: Down onto Gloam. Its air is thinner than Floe's but it will take the edge off a parachute's fall. Where you land decides whether it is noon, dusk or midnight there, for good.

missions.title: The Twilight Tone
missions.text: The hum from Gloam's twilight. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Gloam's surface.
missions.story: On the dusk line, east of the noon point: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Lamp
missions.text: Land in Gloam's twilight by the source and walk a penguin to it.
missions.story: A tall glass lamp, lit, standing where the light always slants. Its glow is the Hearth's warm white. Round its foot the stones are carved with the thread again, and here it forks: one way to Brine, a fierce blue star 5 light-years on, the other to Marrow, an orange star 6.5 light-years off. Two paths, and the builders took both.

missions.title: To Brine
missions.text: Follow one fork of the thread to Brine, a hot blue-white star 5 light-years from Ember.
missions.story: Brine burns nine times brighter than Austra, and far out from it swims Maelstrom: a giant of banded cloud with rings you could drop Floe through, and three moons. Floss throws fountains of ice into space, Selkie has seas and islands and air, Barnacle is all craters. A tone rises from Selkie's islands.

missions.title: Orbit Maelstrom
missions.text: Get into an orbit round Maelstrom whose low point clears its air, 400 km above the cloud tops. Don't go down into the clouds: there is no bottom there, only deeper.

missions.title: Land on Floss
missions.text: Set down near the Fountains, at Floss's south pole, and watch the ice go up.

missions.title: The Tidal Tone
missions.text: The tone from Selkie. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Selkie's surface.
missions.story: An island on Selkie's equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Anchor
missions.text: Land on Selkie's island by the source (mind the sea) and bring a penguin to it.
missions.story: A ring of dark metal sunk deep in the island's rock, and from it a line of light running straight up to Maelstrom, which hangs right overhead here and never moves. The builders moored something here once, and let it go. Carved round the ring is the thread, running on from Brine to a yellow star called Tarn, 4.5 light-years further, and beside Tarn a mark the Archive used for home.

missions.title: To Marrow
missions.text: Follow the thread's other fork to Marrow, an orange star 6.5 light-years from Ember.
missions.story: Marrow's world Saffron is desert from pole to pole: dunes, canyons, towers of red stone and a dead volcano taller than any mountain at home, under a sky the colour of rust. Something in the dunes is ticking.

missions.title: Land on Saffron
missions.text: Down through Saffron's dusty air, less than half as thick as Floe's: try your landing before you trust it.

missions.title: The Ticking
missions.text: The tone from Saffron. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Saffron's surface.
missions.story: In the dune seas south of the equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Hourglass
missions.text: Land in the dunes by the source and walk a penguin to it.
missions.story: A glass the height of a tower, half buried in the dunes, with sand running up through it. The builders' marks on it are a count: how long since they passed this way. It is a very long time. The count's last mark points at Tarn, a yellow star like Austra, and beside it the sign for home.

missions.title: To Tarn
missions.text: Where the thread began, or where its builders did: Tarn, a yellow star 4.5 light-years from Brine.
missions.story: Tarn is Austra's twin, and Mere is what Floe might have been with a little more warmth: sea from pole to pole, scattered with green islands, alive from the beaches to the peaks. On one of the islands something is singing, and it is the Chime's own tone.

missions.title: Land on Mere
missions.text: Set down on one of Mere's islands. There is a lot of sea to miss them in.

missions.title: Home's Tone
missions.text: The singing from Mere. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Mere's surface.
missions.story: An island north of Mere's equator: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Garden
missions.text: Land on the island and walk a penguin to the source.
missions.story: A garden inside a ring of stones, gone wild long ago and still growing. This was home. The stones tell it in the Archive's pictures: the builders lived here, made the Chime and the Keel and the Lamp, and one day all of them left together along the thread to Hollow, 6 light-years on: a star that had already burned out. Nobody leaves a garden like this for a dead star without a reason.

missions.title: To Hollow
missions.text: The last star on the thread: Hollow, 6 light-years from Tarn.
missions.story: Hollow is a white dwarf: the bare, shrinking core of a star that was once like Austra, now not much bigger than a giant planet and still hot enough to glow blue-white. One frozen world goes round it. Cairn has no air, no life and no reason anyone would visit it, and it is covered in the builders' work.

missions.title: Land on Cairn
missions.text: Down onto Cairn's ice. No air at all: engines the whole way.

missions.title: The Last Signal
missions.text: The tone from Cairn. Fly a Signal Scanner where it can see Cairn's surface.
missions.story: Inside the Great Ring: the scanner has it.

missions.title: The Beacon
missions.text: Land inside the Great Ring and walk a penguin to the Beacon.
missions.story: The Beacon stands at the heart of the Great Ring: a needle of the Chime's pale stone a kilometre and a half tall. At the penguin's touch every tone they have followed plays at once, and then one more: an answer, from far out past the edge of every map, in the builders' own voice. They didn't die out and they didn't get lost. They went on, and left the thread so that whoever came after could find them. The next star on it is further than any drive PASA has. For now.

missions.title: Rendezvous
missions.text: Fly within 200 m of another craft in orbit.

missions.title: Docking
missions.text: Dock two craft together.

missions.title: The computer flies
missions.text: Get 1 km up with nobody at the controls: a script on the ship's computer flies it (F2, the Script Editor). Pressing space when a script asks for it is fine.

missions.title: Steady as she goes
missions.text: Hold 50 m above the ground, give or take 2 m, for 20 seconds, the computer at the controls. hover.py in the examples is a start: tune it.

missions.title: Orbit, hands off
missions.text: Reach orbit with your own script flying: no flying keys from the pad to the orbit (to_orbit.py is one way).

missions.title: Krill, hands off
missions.text: Land on Krill with the computer flying all the way from the pad (krill_by_hand.py shows how; doing it your own way pays the same).

missions.title: Who lives on Floe
missions.text: Walk a penguin out among Floe's animals (they keep clear of the pad: go a little way) and get a good look at three kinds of them: walk up close and press E. The shelf penguins will come to you.

missions.title: Kelp's Field Guide
missions.text: On foot on Kelp, get a good look (E) at both of its kinds of animal: the six-legged grazers of the meadows, who run if you rush them, and the drifters floating over them.

missions.title: Not Alone
missions.text: Ships are circling twelve kilometres north of the Lamp, and they aren't the builders'. Bring one down: Tern Laser Turrets (R&D: Lasers) fired by hand, locked on with Shift + click, or by a script of your own (ship.fire_at). They go for anything that comes within a few kilometres of them, and they shoot back.
missions.story: It comes down like any wreck. In what is left of its hull are pieces of the builders' work, cut loose and stacked like salvage: these are the Jaegers, and they have been following the thread too, taking it apart behind them. They keep camps by the builders' places, Gloam's Lamp, Saffron's Hourglass and the Great Ring of Cairn, and they will be back.

missions.title: Safe Ground
missions.text: Dune stalkers hunt Saffron's ergs and badlands. Land a ship with lasers, run a script on its computer that keeps the ground clear (guard.py, or your own), and spend two minutes on foot within 300 m of it without firing a shot yourself.
